entry.content:
Lobsters Top | da.vidbuchanan.co.uk | discussion

A vulnerability in the C2PA (Coalition for Content Provenance and Authenticity) specification allows for file content to be altered after signing without invalidating cryptographic signatures or Time Stamp Authority (TSA) timestamps. By leveraging the "exclusions" feature—which allows specific byte ranges to be omitted from signature calculations—a user can exclude the entire file and sign an empty string. This results in a valid, timestamped signature that covers no data, permitting subsequent modification of the file's contents.

The "exclusion" mechanism is a feature of the C2PA specification designed to accommodate file formats that require post-signature changes, such as updating CRC32 checksums in PNG files. Because current verification tools do not typically flag or restrict the size of these exclusion ranges, the technique allows for the creation of forged, timestamped media. A proposed mitigation involves requiring verifiers to enforce strict, format-specific constraints on which portions of a file are permitted to be excluded from a signature.

entry.title: SequenceHash and SequenceMAC Introduced for Secure Multihashing
entry.content:

Trail of Bits has introduced SequenceHash and SequenceMAC, cryptographic constructions designed for secure multihashing across various hash functions. These tools prevent vulnerabilities caused by ambiguous input encoding and length-extension attacks, which occur when multiple data inputs are concatenated before being hashed. Unlike NIST’s TupleHash, which is tied to Keccak, SequenceHash is hash-agnostic and supports algorithms such as the SHA2 family and BLAKE.

The constructions use a double-hash architecture and a 128-bit length-suffix encoding to ensure semantic distinction between inputs and provide resistance to length-extension. SequenceMAC offers a keyed variant with built-in customization strings for domain separation and protection against key pseudocollisions. Implementations are available in Rust, Go, and Python, and the specification is part of the Community Cryptography Specification Project (C2SP).

entry.title: FunSQL Explains Data-Oriented vs. Syntax-Oriented SQL Query Builders
entry.content:
Lobsters Top | mechanicalrabbit.github.io | discussion

The article distinguishes between two types of SQL query builders: data-oriented and syntax-oriented. Data-oriented builders—such as FunSQL, EF/LINQ, and dbplyr—treat pipeline nodes as sequential data processing steps, meaning the order of operations directly determines the query's output. Conversely, syntax-oriented builders—such as Active Record and Laravel—treat nodes as components for constructing a SQL syntax tree, making the order of assembly irrelevant to the final query.

Syntax-oriented builders are easier to implement but inherit the rigid clause order and grammatical limitations of SQL. Data-oriented builders attempt to represent complex data transformations through query nesting and SQL pushdown, though they may struggle to support the full breadth of SQL's specialized features. FunSQL is designed specifically to expose the complete expressive power of SQL, including recursive queries and lateral joins, by focusing on data processing semantics rather than syntax-driven construction.

entry.title: Deser: An Experimental Rust Serialization Library
entry.content:
Lobsters Top | lucumr.pocoo.org | discussion | hacker news

Deser is an experimental Rust serialization library designed to overcome architectural limitations found in the Serde library. While Serde is type-driven and uses stack recursion, Deser utilizes a format-driven architecture inspired by miniserde, using a heap-allocated driver and sinks to manage state. This design prevents stack overflows and enables suspendable, asynchronous deserialization, allowing data to be parsed as a stream.

The library aims to resolve issues such as information loss during buffering in enums, difficulties with non-self-describing formats, and complex adapter composition. Deser supports formats including JSON, YAML, TOML, and XML, and provides a "layers" middleware system for features like error path tracking and validation. While designed as a potential drop-in replacement for certain use cases, the project currently prioritizes extensibility and completeness.

entry.title: Aho-Corasick Algorithm Construction and Mechanics
entry.content:
Lobsters Top | compiler.club | source | discussion

The Aho-Corasick algorithm enables simultaneous multi-pattern matching within a sequence by constructing a finite state automaton from a trie. It utilizes suffix links to navigate the automaton upon transition failure and output links to identify overlapping pattern matches.

Construction is performed via a breadth-first traversal to compute suffix and output links. These links allow the trie to be determinized into a deterministic finite automaton (DFA), which provides efficient transitions during the pattern-matching process.

entry.title: TimeLord Generates Seeds for Improbable Python Random Sequences
entry.content:
Lobsters Top | github.com | discussion

TimeLord is a Python demonstration that calculates integer seeds required to produce specific, highly improbable sequences from CPython's MT19937 pseudorandom number generator. By representing the generator's twist and temper operations as linear equations over GF(2), the tool works backward from a desired output—such as 1,000 consecutive coin tosses landing on heads or a specific text message—to find a compatible initial seed.

The tool demonstrates the impact of post-selection and selection bias on statistical observations. It shows that an outcome appearing to be a statistical anomaly can be the result of a seed being chosen specifically to achieve that result, rather than an inherent property of a random process. The resulting seeds are fully compatible with the standard Python `random.Random` class, allowing for the reproduction of these sequences without modifying the core library.
